summary:
Mimizuku is an interactive web app that transforms NASA's Earth imagery and scientific data into sound. By moving across a map, users can hear changes in Earth's patterns in real time, explore different datasets, and create their own musical experience.

Mimizuku offers a playful new way to discover our planet. Our goal is to make Earth science more engaging and approachable for everyone, while exploring new possibilities for experiencing information beyond sight.
details:
What it does / How it works

Mimizuku lets people explore NASA's Earth imagery and scientific data through an interactive map that turns visual patterns into sound.

Users can choose from 13 datasets covering ocean color, air pollution, temperature, and other Earth phenomena. As they move or zoom the map, Mimizuku analyzes the image inside a square listening area and generates sound that changes with the visual patterns. Users can also choose from 32 sound presets to personalize their experience.

Behind the scenes, we use a two-dimensional Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to analyze image textures and convert them into musical harmonics. The overall color influences the base pitch, while spatial audio places RGB color channels in different directions. Numerical data is first visualized as colored maps and processed in the same way.

All sound is generated directly in the browser, responding dynamically as users explore.

Benefits

Mimizuku makes Earth data more approachable by turning exploration into an interactive listening experience. Users can discover changes in visual patterns, compare locations, and experiment with different sounds without needing scientific expertise.

The app also supports keyboard navigation, screen readers, and internationalization, helping more people participate in Earth exploration.

Intended impact

Earth science is often communicated through visualizations that rely heavily on sight. We want to explore another way to experience this information.

By combining Earth data with sound and creativity, Mimizuku aims to make scientific exploration more engaging and inclusive, especially for people who are blind or have low vision.

We hope to inspire curiosity about our planet and encourage more people to explore NASA's Earth information.

Tools and technologies

  • Frontend: TypeScript, Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and React Aria Components.
  • Audio: Web Audio API for sound generation and spatial audio, with FFT analysis in a Web Worker.
  • Data: NASA SVS imagery, GEOS-CF atmospheric and weather data, and NASA JPL MUR sea-surface temperature.
  • Infrastructure: Cloudflare R2 for data storage and Cloudflare Workers for application delivery.

Creativity

We started with a simple question: What if we could turn the patterns of Earth into music?

Inspired by frequency-based image processing, we developed a way to transform image textures and colors into musical soundscapes.

Instead of listening to a fixed composition, users shape the music themselves by exploring different locations, switching datasets, and choosing sound presets.

We wanted to combine scientific information with creative expression, making Earth exploration feel like discovering something through play.

Factors we considered

Accessibility: We implemented keyboard navigation, screen-reader support, and multilingual interfaces. With blind and low-vision users in mind, we also tested the experience using a screen reader to evaluate usability without relying on sight.

Mobile experience: We designed the interface to work across desktop and mobile devices, considering different screen sizes and touch interactions so users can explore Earth data wherever they are.

Real-time performance: To ensure sound responds smoothly as users explore the map, we optimized audio generation and used Web Workers to handle computationally intensive image analysis without interrupting user interactions.

Efficient data delivery: Earth observation datasets can be massive, so we optimized data processing and delivery to reduce browser loading times. By utilizing Cloudflare R2 and Workers, we aim to provide a fast and responsive experience for users around the world.
